title: Composition of regular ring maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be regular ring maps [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of commutative rings. If for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of the composite $A\to C$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], then the composite $A\to C$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QI (more-algebra-lemma-regular-composition, line 10440); its proof uses Lemma 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change) and algebra.tex lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre, 'some details omitted'

proof.text: Compose flatness of A → B and B → C using RingHom.Flat.comp and the scalar-tower equality.

Fix a prime p of A and a finite purely inseparable K/κ(p). The field extension is finitely generated. Apply the existing geometric regularity field-extension theorem to p.Fiber B to obtain regularity of D=K⊗[κ(p)](p.Fiber B). This avoids the universe mismatch between the finite-extension quantifier for B and the one for C. The Noetherian hypothesis gives p.Fiber C Noetherian; Module.Finite.base_change and IsNoetherianRing.of_finite, followed by tensor symmetry, give E=K⊗[κ(p)](p.Fiber C) Noetherian.

Tensor the flat upper map twice using RingHom.Flat.lTensor to obtain flatness of D → E. Apply the extended-fibre theorem to obtain regularity of every fibre of this map. The flat ascent theorem gives regularity of E. This holds for every finite purely inseparable K, so the composite fibre is geometrically regular. Combine with Noetherianity and flatness to conclude regularity of A → C.
